mishnayos.summary: Everyone must come to the Beis HaMikdash on the three Yamim Tovim to "be seen" there with a korban, except some people the mishnah lists. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about which small child must come.

chunks.en: Everyone must come to be seen in the Beis HaMikdash on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: This mitzvah is called re'iyah, being seen.
chunks.st: All are obligated on the three pilgrim Festivals in the mitzva of appearance, i.e., to appear in the Temple as well as to sacrifice an offering,

words.note: The mitzvah to come to the Beis HaMikdash on Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos and bring a korban.

chunks.en: except a person who cannot hear or speak,
chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

words.note: A person who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a person whose mind is not well, and a small child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, and a minor;

words.note: A person whose mind does not work properly.
A child who is not yet bar mitzvah.

chunks.en: a tumtum and an androginos,
chunks.st: and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite,

words.note: A person whom we cannot tell is a boy or a girl.
A person who seems to be both a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: women, and slaves who were not set free,
chunks.st: and women, and slaves who are not emancipated;

chunks.en: someone who cannot walk well, and a blind person,
chunks.st: and the lame, and the blind,

chunks.en: a sick person, and an old person,
chunks.st: and the sick, and the old,

chunks.en: and anyone who cannot go up to Yerushalayim on his own feet.
chunks.st: and one who is unable to ascend to Jerusalem on his own legs.

chunks.en: Which child counts as "a small child" who does not have to come?
chunks.st: Who has the status of a minor with regard to this halakha?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִרְכּוֹב עַל כְּתֵפָיו
chunks.en: Any child who cannot ride on the shoulders
chunks.st: Any child who is unable to ride on his father’s shoulders

chunks.he: שֶׁל אָבִיו וְלַעֲלוֹת מִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: of his father and go up from Yerushalayim to Har HaBayis.
chunks.st: and ascend from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount;

words.note: Har HaBayis is the mountain where the Beis HaMikdash stood.

chunks.en: That is what Beis Shammai say.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Beit Shammai.

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of Shammai.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

words.note: Beis Hillel are the students of Hillel.

chunks.en: Any child who cannot hold
chunks.st: Any child who is unable to hold

chunks.en: his father's hand
chunks.st: his father’s hand

chunks.en: and walk up from Yerushalayim to Har HaBayis.
chunks.st: and ascend on foot from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount,

chunks.en: Because the Torah says "three regalim."
chunks.explain: Regel also means foot: you go up on your feet.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Three times [regalim]” (Exodus 23:14).
chunks.stMore: Since the term for feet is raglayim, Beit Hillel infer from here that the obligation to ascend involves the use of one’s legs.

words.note: Times, or Yamim Tovim; the word sounds like raglayim, feet.

mishnayos.summary: How much money must be spent on the re'iyah korban and the chagigah korban? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: The re'iyah korban must cost at least two silver coins,
chunks.st: The burnt-offering of appearance brought on a pilgrim Festival must be worth at least two silver coins,

words.note: An olah korban brought when coming to be seen in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and the chagigah korban at least one silver ma'ah.
chunks.st: and the Festival peace-offering must be worth at least one silver ma’a coin.

words.note: A shelamim korban brought for the Yom Tov and eaten in celebration.
A small silver coin.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: The re'iyah korban must cost at least one silver ma'ah,
chunks.st: The burnt-offering of appearance must be worth at least one silver ma’a

chunks.en: and the chagigah korban at least two silver coins.
chunks.st: and the Festival peace-offering at least two silver coins.

mishnayos.summary: Which money may be used to buy the Yom Tov korbanos? Olos must be bought with regular money, but shelamim may be bought with maaser sheni money.

chunks.en: Olos brought on Yom Tov must be bought with regular money,
chunks.explain: Not with maaser sheni money, which is holy.
chunks.st: Burnt-offerings that one sacrifices on the intermediate days of the Festival must come from non-sacred property,
chunks.stMore: not from sacred property such as second-tithe money.

words.note: Korbanos that are burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: but the shelamim may come from maaser money.
chunks.st: But the peace-offerings may be brought from the second tithe,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from money with which one redeemed second tithe, which is subsequently used to purchase food in Jerusalem.

words.note: Korbanos that are mostly eaten by the people who bring them.
Maaser sheni: money used to buy food to eat in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: About the chagigah of the first day of Pesach,
chunks.st: With regard to the Festival peace-offering sacrificed on the first day of the festival of Passover,

words.note: Yom Tov means a holiday.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: it must come from regular money.
chunks.st: It must come from non-sacred property,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: It may come from maaser money.
chunks.st: It may be brought even from the second tithe.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov there is a mitzvah to be happy by eating meat of korbanos. This mishnah teaches which korbanos count for this mitzvah.

chunks.en: Regular Jews do their mitzvah of being happy on Yom Tov
chunks.st: In general, Israelites fulfill their obligation to eat peace-offerings of rejoicing

words.note: Jews who are not Kohanim.

chunks.en: with korbanos they promised to bring, and with maaser animals.
chunks.st: with their voluntary vows and gift offerings donated during the year and sacrificed on the Festival; and likewise with animal tithes.

words.note: Every tenth animal born was brought as a korban.

chunks.en: And the Kohanim do it with chatas and asham korbanos,
chunks.st: And the priests fulfill their obligation of rejoicing with the meat of sin-offerings and guilt-offerings

words.note: Korbanos brought for some sins; the Kohanim eat them.
Another kind of korban for a sin; the Kohanim eat them.

chunks.en: with the bechor, and with the chest and leg they get from shelamim.
chunks.st: and with firstborn offerings, as the priests receive a portion of these, and with the breast and thigh of peace-offerings, to which they are also entitled.

words.note: A firstborn animal, given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: But not with birds and not with flour korbanos.
chunks.explain: Only eating meat counts as being happy.
chunks.st: However, they do not fulfill their obligation with birds, e.g., a bird sacrificed as a sin-offering, nor with meal-offerings,
chunks.stMore: as only the eating of meat constitutes rejoicing.

words.note: Korbanos made of flour.

mishnayos.summary: A person with a big family should bring more shelamim to feed them, and a rich person with a small family should bring more olos. A person who has a lot should give a lot.

chunks.en: Someone who has many people to feed
chunks.st: One who has many eaters, i.e., members of his household,

chunks.en: and only a little money
chunks.st: and a small amount of property,

chunks.en: brings many shelamim and few olos.
chunks.explain: He can feed his family from the shelamim.
chunks.st: may bring many peace-offerings and few burnt-offerings,
chunks.stMore: so he can feed the members of his household with the peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has lots of money and few people to feed,
chunks.st: If one has much property and few eaters,

chunks.en: he brings many olos and few shelamim.
chunks.st: he should bring many burnt-offerings and few peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has little of both,
chunks.st: If both these and those, his property and the members of his household, are few,

chunks.en: about him the Rabbis said
chunks.st: with regard to this individual it is stated in the mishna (2a)

chunks.en: one silver ma'ah and two silver coins.
chunks.explain: The smallest amounts taught in the mishnah before.
chunks.st: that the Sages established the smallest amount of one silver ma’a for the burnt-offering of appearance in the Temple and two silver coins for the Festival peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has a lot of both,
chunks.st: If both his eaters and his property are many,

chunks.en: about him the Torah says:
chunks.st: with regard to this individual it is stated:

chunks.en: "Each man as he can give, like the bracha of Hashem
chunks.st: “Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord

chunks.en: your G-d which He gave you."
chunks.st: your God, which He has given you” (Deuteronomy 16:17).

mishnayos.summary: If someone did not bring his chagigah korban on the first day of Yom Tov, he can still bring it later in the Yom Tov. Once Yom Tov is over, he can no longer make it up.

chunks.en: Someone who did not bring his chagigah korban
chunks.st: With regard to one who did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering

chunks.en: on the first day of Sukkos,
chunks.st: on the first day of the festival of Sukkot,

words.note: Sukkos.

chunks.en: may bring it all the rest of the Yom Tov
chunks.st: he may celebrate and bring it during the entire remaining days of the pilgrimage Festival,

words.note: The Yom Tov.

chunks.en: and even on the last day, Shemini Atzeres.
chunks.st: and even on the final day of the Festival, i.e., on the Eighth Day of Assembly.

chunks.en: If the Yom Tov passed and he did not bring it,
chunks.st: If the pilgrimage Festival passed and one did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering,

chunks.en: he does not have to make it up.
chunks.explain: It is too late; the chance for the mitzvah is gone.
chunks.st: he is not obligated to pay restitution for it.
chunks.stMore: Even if he consecrated an animal for this purpose and it was lost, once the Festival is over he has no obligation to replace it, as he has missed the opportunity for performing this mitzva.

chunks.en: About this the pasuk says:
chunks.st: And about this it is stated:

chunks.en: "Something crooked cannot be made straight,
chunks.st: “That which is crooked cannot be made straight;

chunks.en: and something missing cannot be counted."
chunks.st: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered” (Ecclesiastes 1:15).

mishnayos.summary: Two Rabbis explain the pasuk "something crooked cannot be made straight." Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says it means a talmid chacham who stops learning Torah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
What is the crooked thing that cannot be fixed?
This is someone who did a forbidden relationship
and a mamzer was born from it.
chunks.explain: A mamzer's status can never be changed.

words.note: A child born from a forbidden relationship; his status stays forever.

chunks.en: If you say it means someone who steals or robs,
he can give it back and fix what he did.
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
We call something crooked only if
it was straight at first and then became crooked.

chunks.he: וְאֵיזֶה, זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה:
chunks.en: And who is this? A talmid chacham who leaves the Torah.

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

mishnayos.summary: Some parts of Torah have only a tiny hint in the pasukim but many halachos, and some have a strong source in the Torah. The ones with a strong source are the main parts of the Torah.

chunks.en: The halachos of undoing a neder fly in the air,
chunks.st: The halakhot of the dissolution of vows, when one requests from a Sage to dissolve them, fly in the air

words.note: Promises a person makes, which a Rav can undo.

chunks.en: and have almost nothing in the Torah to lean on.
chunks.explain: The Torah only hints at them.
chunks.st: and have nothing to support them,
chunks.stMore: as these halakhot are not mentioned explicitly in the Torah. There is only a slight allusion to the dissolution of vows in the Torah, which is taught by the Sages as part of the oral tradition.

chunks.en: The halachos of Shabbos,
chunks.st: The halakhot of Shabbat,

chunks.en: chagigah korbanos, and me'ilah,
chunks.st: Festival peace-offerings, and misuse of consecrated property

words.note: Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: are like mountains hanging by a hair,
chunks.st: are like mountains suspended by a hair,

chunks.en: because they have few pesukim and many halachos.
chunks.st: as they have little written about them in the Torah, and yet the details of their halakhot are numerous.

chunks.en: The laws of judging and the avodah in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: The details of monetary law, sacrificial rites,

words.note: Laws a beis din judges, like money cases.
The service in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: tahara, tumah, and forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: ritual purity and impurity, and the halakhot of those with whom relations are forbidden

words.note: Relatives a person may not marry.

chunks.en: have something in the Torah to lean on.
chunks.st: all have something to support them, i.e., there is ample basis in the Torah for these halakhot,

chunks.en: They are the main parts of the Torah.
chunks.st: and these are the essential parts of Torah.

mishnayos.stIntro: Incidental to the Festival peace-offering, the mishna describes the nature of various areas of Torah study.

mishnayos.summary: Some very deep and holy parts of the Torah may be taught only to a few students at a time, and only to a wise student. A person must not try to dig into things Hashem did not let us know.

chunks.en: We do not teach the hidden halachos of forbidden relationships to three students together,

words.note: Relatives a person may not marry.

chunks.en: nor the secrets of how Hashem created the world to two,

words.note: The creation of the world.

chunks.en: nor the Merkavah even to one student,
chunks.explain: The Merkavah is a very holy, secret vision of Hashem's "chariot."

words.note: The vision of Hashem's chariot that the navi Yechezkel saw.

chunks.en: unless he is
wise and understands things on his own.
Anyone who looks into four things,

chunks.he: רָאוּי לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ לֹא בָּא לָעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: it would be better for him if he had not come into the world:
what is above the sky,
what is below the earth,
what was before the world was made,
and what will be after the world ends.

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ,
chunks.en: And anyone who does not care about the honor of his Creator,
it would be better for him if he had not come into the world.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the pairs of great Rabbis who led the Jewish people, and how each one ruled about doing semichah, leaning one's hands on a korban, on Yom Tov.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yosei ben Yoezer says not to do semichah on Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: Semichah is leaning your hands on a korban before it is shechted.
chunks.st: Yosei ben Yo’ezer says not to place one’s hands on offerings before slaughtering them on a Festival
chunks.stMore: because this is considered performing labor with an animal on a Festival.

words.note: To lean hands on a korban (semichah).

chunks.en: Yosei ben Yochanan says to do semichah.
chunks.st: His colleague, Yosef ben Yoḥanan, says to place them;

chunks.he: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yehoshua ben Perachyah says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Yehoshua ben Peraḥya says not to place them;

chunks.en: Nitai HaArbeli says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Nitai HaArbeli says to place them;

words.note: A town in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טַבַּאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yehudah ben Tabai says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Yehuda ben Tabbai says not to place them;

chunks.en: Shimon ben Shatach says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shimon ben Shataḥ says to place them;

chunks.en: Shemayah says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shemaya says to place them;

chunks.en: Avtalyon says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Avtalyon says not to place them.

chunks.en: Hillel and Menachem did not argue.
chunks.st: Hillel and Menaḥem did not disagree with regard to this issue.

chunks.en: Menachem left his job,
chunks.st: Menaḥem departed from his post,

chunks.en: and Shammai came in his place.
chunks.st: and Shammai entered in his stead.

chunks.en: Shammai says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shammai says not to place them;

chunks.en: Hillel says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Hillel says to place them.

chunks.en: The first one of each pair was the Nasi,
chunks.st: The first members of each pair served as Nasi,

words.note: The Nasi was the head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: and the second one was the Av Beis Din, the next in charge.
chunks.st: and their counterparts served as deputy Nasi.

words.note: Av Beis Din: the second leader of the Sanhedrin.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about which korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov, and whether we may lean our hands on them.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim on Yom Tov, but we do not do semichah on them,
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings on a Festival because both the owners and the priests partake of them, but one may not place his hands on them,
chunks.stMore: on the peace-offerings before sacrificing them.

chunks.en: but we may not bring olos.
chunks.explain: Olos are not eaten, and on Yom Tov we work only to make food.
chunks.st: However, one may not bring burnt-offerings
chunks.stMore: at all because they are not eaten, and labor is permitted on Festivals only for the sake of preparing food for humans.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim and olos, and we do semichah on them.
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings and also burnt-offerings, and one places his hands on both of them.

mishnayos.summary: When Shavuos comes on Erev Shabbos or on Shabbos, the Yom Tov korbanos may be brought on Sunday. On that Sunday the Kohen Gadol did not wear his special clothes, to show that Shavuos is not always on Sunday.

chunks.en: When Shavuos falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the festival of Shavuot occurs on the eve of Shabbat,

words.note: Shavuos.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: the day for shechting the korbanos is after Shabbos.
chunks.explain: They hold the Yom Tov olah is not brought on Yom Tov itself.
chunks.st: The day of slaughter is after Shabbat, on Sunday.
chunks.stMore: This is the day on which the animals brought in honor of the pilgrim Festival are slaughtered, since they maintain that the Festival burnt-offering is not sacrificed on the Festival day itself but on the following day, and all burnt-offerings vowed by individuals are postponed to the following day.

words.note: The day the Yom Tov korbanos are brought.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: There is no shechting day after Shabbos.
chunks.explain: The korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov itself.
chunks.st: The day of slaughter is not after Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: Since the slaughter may be performed on the Festival day itself, it is unnecessary to postpone it.

chunks.en: But they agree that if Shavuos falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: But they concede that if Shavuot occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: the shechting day is after Shabbos.
chunks.st: the day of slaughter is after Shabbat.

chunks.en: On that day the Kohen Gadol does not put on his special clothes,
chunks.st: The mishna relates that when the day of slaughter was on a Sunday, the High Priest would not dress in his festive garments
chunks.stMore: but would wear his regular clothing.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol is the head Kohen.

chunks.en: and people may give hespedim and fast on it,
chunks.st: And all were permitted to eulogize and fast on this day.

words.note: A speech of sadness for someone who died.

chunks.en: so as not to support the words of those who say
chunks.explain: These were people who did not believe in the Torah she'baal peh.
chunks.st: This was done in order not to uphold and reinforce the opinion of the Sadducees, who would say:

chunks.en: Shavuos is always after Shabbos.
chunks.st: Shavuot must always occur after Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: As the day of slaughter was on Sunday, it was necessary to demonstrate that we do not accept the view of the Sadducees, and that the day is not a Festival.

mishnayos.summary: There are different levels of tahara for different kinds of holy food. For regular food we wash our hands, but for korbanos we dip our hands in a mikveh.

chunks.en: We wash hands for regular food, for maaser, and for terumah.
chunks.st: One must wash his hands by pouring a quarter-log of water over them before eating non-sacred food, and for tithes and for teruma;

chunks.en: But for korbanos, we dip the hands in a mikveh.
chunks.st: but for eating sacrificial food one must immerse one’s hands in purification waters, such as those of a ritual bath.

words.note: Holy food of korbanos.

chunks.en: And for the parah adumah water, if his hands became tamei,
chunks.st: And with regard to one who wishes to touch the purification waters of the red heifer used for sprinkling, concerning which the Sages ordained further measures of sanctity, if one’s hands were rendered impure
chunks.stMore: even by rabbinical ritual impurity, which usually only renders the hands impure,

words.note: The special water made with the ashes of the parah adumah.

chunks.en: his whole body becomes tamei.
chunks.st: his entire body is rendered impure, and he must immerse himself in a ritual bath.

mishnayos.summary: When a person goes to the mikveh, he becomes tahor only for the level of holy food he had in mind. If he had in mind a holier level, he may also eat the less holy foods.

chunks.en: Someone who toveled for regular food and is counted tahor for regular food
chunks.st: If one immersed for the purpose of eating non-sacred food, he assumes a presumptive status of ritual purity for non-sacred food,

words.note: Dips in a mikveh to become tahor.

chunks.en: may not eat maaser.
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for him to eat tithes,
chunks.stMore: as he did not purify himself with the intention of eating tithes.

chunks.en: If he toveled for maaser and is counted tahor for maaser,
chunks.st: If one immersed to eat tithes, he assumes a presumptive status for tithes,

chunks.en: he may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from eating teruma.

chunks.en: If he toveled for terumah
chunks.st: If one immersed for teruma,

chunks.en: and is counted tahor for terumah,
chunks.st: he assumes a presumptive status for teruma,

chunks.en: he may not eat korbanos.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from eating sacrificial food.

chunks.en: If he toveled for korbanos and is counted tahor for korbanos,
chunks.st: If he immersed for sacrificial food, he assumes a presumptive status for sacrificial food,

chunks.en: he may not touch the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from coming in contact with the purification waters.

chunks.en: If he toveled for something stricter,
chunks.st: The principle is as follows: One who immersed to eat a food in a stringent category

chunks.en: he may have something less strict.
chunks.st: is permitted to eat a food in a lenient one.

chunks.en: If he toveled but did not have in mind to become tahor,
chunks.st: Another principle: One who immersed without the intention to assume a presumptive status of ritual purity, i.e., one who immersed but did not intend to purify himself,

chunks.en: it is as if he did not tovel.
chunks.st: it is as though he has not immersed at all.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues to list additional differences between various levels of ritual purity:

mishnayos.summary: People who keep a higher level of tahara must be careful with the clothes of people who keep a lower level. Even the clothes of very careful tzaddikim were counted as tamei for holier things.

chunks.en: The clothes of an am ha'aretz are tamei with midras for perushim.
chunks.explain: Perushim are people very careful about tahara.
chunks.st: The garments of an am ha’aretz, one who is not careful with regard to the laws of ritual purity, are considered impure with the ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav. That is considered a primary level of impurity for individuals who are scrupulous with regard to impurity [perushin].

words.note: Am ha'aretz: a person who is not careful about tumah and tahara.
A strong kind of tumah, like a seat a zav sat on.

chunks.en: The clothes of perushim are tamei with midras for those who eat terumah.
chunks.st: The garments of perushin are considered impure by the treading of a zav for priests who eat teruma;

chunks.en: The clothes of those who eat terumah are tamei with midras for korbanos.
chunks.st: the garments of those who eat teruma are considered impure by the treading of a zav for those who eat sacrificial food;

chunks.en: The clothes of those who eat korbanos are tamei with midras for the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: and likewise the garments of those who eat sacrificial food are considered impure by the treading of a zav for those dealing with the preparation of the purification waters.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיָה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: Yosef ben Yoezer was the most pious of the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The mishna relates: Yosef ben Yo’ezer was the most pious member of the priesthood
chunks.stMore: and was extremely careful to eat teruma in a state of ritual purity,

chunks.en: and still his cloth was tamei with midras for korbanos.
chunks.st: and yet his cloth was considered impure by the treading of a zav for those who ate sacrificial food.

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Gudgeda ate
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda would eat non-sacred food

chunks.en: his regular food as carefully as korbanos all his life,
chunks.st: while following the laws of ritual purity for sacrificial food all his days,

chunks.en: and still his cloth was tamei with midras for the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: and nevertheless his cloth was considered impure by the treading of a zav for those preparing the purification waters.

mishnayos.summary: Kodesh, the food of korbanos, has stricter rules of tahara than terumah. This mishnah lists some of those stricter rules.

chunks.en: Kodesh has stricter rules than terumah:

words.note: Holy food of korbanos.
A gift of food for the Kohanim.

chunks.en: for terumah we may tovel keilim inside other keilim,

words.note: Dip in a mikveh to make tahor.
Dishes, pots and tools.

chunks.en: but not for kodesh.
For terumah, the outside, inside and handle of a kli count as separate parts,
chunks.explain: If one part becomes tamei, the other parts stay tahor.

words.note: The handle, where you hold the kli.

chunks.en: but not for kodesh.

chunks.he: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַמִּדְרָס נוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: Someone carrying something with midras tumah may also carry terumah,

words.note: Something with a strong kind of tumah, like a seat a zav sat on.

chunks.en: but not kodesh.
The clothes of those who eat terumah
are counted as midras for kodesh.
The rule of terumah is not like the rule of kodesh:
for kodesh, he unties a knot, dries it, and tovels it,
chunks.explain: A knot or wetness could keep the mikveh water from reaching everywhere.

chunks.en: and only after that ties it again;
but for terumah, he may tie it and then tovel it.

mishnayos.summary: More stricter rules for kodesh than for terumah: about new keilim, food in one kli, levels of tumah, and tamei hands.

chunks.en: Keilim that were finished being made while tahor
chunks.st: Vessels that were fashioned and completed in purity

chunks.en: must be toveled before using them for kodesh,
chunks.st: nevertheless require immersion to be considered pure for sacrificial foods,

words.note: Dipping in a mikveh.

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not for teruma.

chunks.en: A kli joins together all the food inside it for kodesh,
chunks.explain: If one piece becomes tamei, all the pieces become tamei.
chunks.st: A vessel combines all the food that is in it with regard to sacrificial food,
chunks.stMore: meaning that if one piece of food becomes impure all the other pieces become impure as well;

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not with regard to teruma,
chunks.stMore: concerning which each piece is treated independently.

chunks.en: Kodesh can become pasul even at the fourth level of tumah,
chunks.explain: Tumah passes from thing to thing in steps, called levels.
chunks.st: The mishna continues the list of differences between sacrificial food and teruma. Sacrificial food that is impure with fourth-degree impurity is disqualified,
chunks.stMore: meaning that the sacrificial food is rendered impure but it does not impart impurity to other items.

words.note: The fourth level, or step, of tumah.
No longer fit to eat.

chunks.en: but terumah only up to the third level.
chunks.st: Teruma is disqualified when it is impure with third-degree impurity;
chunks.stMore: it is not susceptible to fourth-degree impurity at all.

chunks.en: And for terumah, if one of his hands became tamei,
chunks.st: And with regard to teruma, if one of one’s hands became impure
chunks.stMore: by rabbinic law that renders only the hands impure,

chunks.en: the other hand is still tahor.
chunks.st: its counterpart, i.e., the other hand, remains pure.

chunks.en: But for kodesh, he must tovel both hands,
chunks.st: But with regard to sacrificial food, if one hand becomes impure he must immerse them both,

chunks.en: because one hand makes the other hand tamei for kodesh,
chunks.st: as one hand renders its counterpart impure with regard to sacrificial food

chunks.en: but not for terumah.
chunks.st: but not with regard to teruma.

mishnayos.summary: More differences between kodesh and terumah: about eating dry food with tamei hands, and about people who must go to the mikveh before eating kodesh.

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין אֳכָלִים נְגוּבִין בְּיָדַיִם מְסֹאָבוֹת בַּתְּרוּמָה,
chunks.en: We may eat dry foods with tamei hands when it is terumah,
chunks.explain: Dry food cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: One may eat dry foods, i.e., foods that have never come into contact with liquid and are therefore not susceptible to impurity, with impure hands when it is teruma,

chunks.en: but not when it is kodesh.
chunks.st: but not when it is sacrificial food.

chunks.en: An onen and someone who still has to bring a korban to finish becoming tahor
chunks.st: An acute mourner [onen], i.e., someone who has experienced the loss of a close relative on that day, who had not come into contact with the deceased; and one who is lacking atonement, i.e., someone who still needs to bring an offering to complete his purification procedure, such as a zav or a woman after childbirth,

words.note: Someone whose close relative died that day.
Someone who still needs to bring a korban to finish becoming tahor.

chunks.en: must go to the mikveh before eating kodesh,
chunks.st: both require immersion in order to eat sacrificial food.
chunks.stMore: The onen would immerse after the day has passed and the one lacking atonement would immerse after the requisite offering is brought.

chunks.en: but not before eating terumah.
chunks.st: However, immersion in these cases is not necessary for eating teruma.

mishnayos.summary: Terumah also has some stricter rules than kodesh. People who are not careful about tahara are believed about kodesh all year, but about terumah only at the time of making wine and oil.

chunks.en: Terumah is stricter in this way:
chunks.st: stringencies that apply to teruma over sacrificial food:

chunks.en: In Yehudah, everyone is believed that wine
chunks.explain: Even an am ha'aretz, who is not careful about tumah.
chunks.st: In Judea all people, even people who are not generally meticulous in their observance of the halakhot of ritual purity [amei ha’aretz], are trusted with regard to the purity of consecrated wine

chunks.en: and oil for the Beis HaMikdash are tahor, all year long.
chunks.st: and oil throughout all the days of the year.

chunks.he: וּבִשְׁעַת הַגִּתּוֹת וְהַבַּדִּים אַף עַל הַתְּרוּמָה.
chunks.en: And at the time of making wine and oil, they are believed even about terumah.
chunks.explain: Then everyone makes his keilim tahor.
chunks.st: And during the period of the winepress and olive press, when grapes and olives are pressed and made into wine and oil, respectively, they are trusted even with regard to the purity of teruma,
chunks.stMore: as all people, including amei ha’aretz, purify their vessels for this season.

chunks.en: If the time of making wine and oil passed, and someone brought a Kohen
chunks.st: But once the periods of the winepress and olive press have passed, if amei ha’aretz brought to him, i.e., to a priest who is meticulous concerning the halakhot of ritual purity [ḥaver],

chunks.en: a barrel of terumah wine,
chunks.st: a barrel of teruma wine,

chunks.en: the Kohen should not take it from him.
chunks.st: he may not accept it from them,
chunks.stMore: as amei ha’aretz are not trusted with regard to matters of ritual purity during the rest of the year.

chunks.en: But he may leave it for the next wine-making time.
chunks.st: But the giver may leave it over for the following winepress season,
chunks.stMore: in the following year, at which point the ḥaver priest may accept it from him, although it was prohibited for him to accept the same barrel beforehand.

chunks.en: And if he told the Kohen,
chunks.st: And if the giver said to the priest:

chunks.en: "I put a revi'is of kodesh into it," he is believed.
chunks.explain: He is believed about kodesh, so also about the terumah with it.
chunks.st: I separated and placed into this barrel of teruma a quarter-log of sacrificial wine or oil, he is trusted
chunks.stMore: with regard to the entire contents of the barrel. Since an am ha’aretz is trusted with regard to the purity of sacrificial food, he is also believed with regard to teruma that is mingled with the sacrificial food.

words.note: A small measure, about a cup.

chunks.en: Jugs of wine and jugs of oil that have terumah mixed in:
chunks.st: With regard to jugs of wine and jugs of oil that are mingled,

chunks.en: people are believed about them at the time of making wine and oil,
chunks.st: amei ha’aretz are trusted with regard to them during the period of the winepress and the olive press,

chunks.en: and for seventy days before the wine-making time.
chunks.st: and also up to seventy days before the winepress,
chunks.stMore: for that is when people begin to purify their vessels in preparation for the wine-pressing season.

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna listed stringencies that apply to sacrificial food but not to teruma. However, there are also

mishnayos.summary: Near Yerushalayim, up to the town of Modi'im, every potter is believed that his clay pots are tahor. Farther away, a potter who is not careful is not believed.

chunks.en: From Modi'im and in, toward Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: From Modi’im and inward toward Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in the area surrounding Jerusalem, up to the distance of the town of Modi’im, which is fifteen mil from Jerusalem,

words.note: A town fifteen mil from Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: potters are believed about clay keilim.
chunks.st: all potters, including amei ha’aretz, are deemed credible with regard to the purity of earthenware vessels that they have produced.
chunks.stMore: Because these places supplied earthenware vessels for the people in Jerusalem, the Sages did not decree impurity for them.

chunks.en: From Modi'im and farther out,
chunks.st: From Modi’im and outward, however,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.en: How is this? A potter who sells pots
chunks.st: The details of this ruling are specified: How so? A potter who sells pots,

chunks.en: came in past Modi'im:
chunks.st: if he entered within Modi’im from outside it,

chunks.he: הוּא הַקַּדָּר וְהֵן הַקְּדֵרוֹת וְהֵן הַלּוֹקְחִים, נֶאֱמָן.
chunks.en: the same potter, the same pots and the same buyers, he is believed.
chunks.explain: Even though they all came from outside Modi'im.
chunks.st: although the potter, and the pots, and the customers were all previously located outside Modi’im, where he is not deemed credible with regard to purity, he is now deemed credible.

chunks.en: If he went out, he is not believed.
chunks.st: And the opposite is true of the opposite case: If the same person who was deemed credible inside left the boundaries of Modi’im, he is no longer deemed credible.

mishnayos.summary: Tax collectors or thieves who say they did not touch anything are believed. In Yerushalayim everyone is believed about kodesh, and on Yom Tov even about terumah.

chunks.en: Tax collectors who came into a house,
chunks.st: In the case of amei ha’aretz tax collectors who entered a house to collect items for a tax,

chunks.en: and also thieves who brought back the keilim,
chunks.st: and similarly thieves who returned the vessels they had stolen,

chunks.en: are believed when they say,
chunks.st: they are deemed credible when they say:

chunks.en: "We did not touch the other things."
chunks.st: We did not touch
chunks.stMore: the rest of the objects in the house, and those items remain pure.

chunks.en: And in Yerushalayim everyone is believed about kodesh,
chunks.st: And in Jerusalem all people, even amei ha’aretz, are deemed credible with regard to sacrificial food throughout the year,

chunks.en: and at the time of the Yom Tov, even about terumah.
chunks.st: and during a pilgrimage Festival they are deemed credible even with regard to teruma.

words.note: The Yom Tov when everyone came to Yerushalayim.

mishnayos.summary: During Yom Tov everyone is counted as tahor, so after Yom Tov the keilim of the Beis HaMikdash were made tahor again. The mishnah also says when this was done.

chunks.en: Someone who opens his barrel of wine to sell,
chunks.st: In the case of one who opens his barrel of wine for public sale,

chunks.en: or starts selling his dough during Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: People who are not careful about tahara touched it.
chunks.st: and similarly one who starts selling his dough during the time of the pilgrimage Festival, and these items perforce come into contact with amei ha’aretz,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says: he may finish selling it after Yom Tov.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Since the food was pure, despite its contact with amei ha’aretz, when he began selling it, he may finish selling it in a state of purity even after the Festival,
chunks.stMore: and there is no concern about the contact that has been made by amei ha’aretz during the Festival.

chunks.en: And the Sages say: he may not finish.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say: He may not finish selling it.

chunks.en: Once Yom Tov was over,
chunks.st: Once the pilgrimage Festival has passed by,

chunks.en: they would make the keilim of the Azarah tahor again.
chunks.explain: Many people had touched them during Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the priests pass all the vessels of the Temple courtyard through a process of purification,
chunks.stMore: since they were touched by am ha’aretz priests during the Festival.

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: If Yom Tov ended and the next day was Friday,
chunks.st: If the Festival passed by into a Friday, i.e., if the Festival ended on Thursday night,

chunks.en: they would not do it then,
chunks.st: they would not pass the vessels through the purification process on that day,

chunks.en: because of the honor of Shabbos.
chunks.st: due to the honor of Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: in order to give the priests time to prepare the requirements of Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Not even on Thursday,
chunks.st: They do not even purify them on Thursday,
chunks.stMore: in the event that the Festival ended on Wednesday night,

chunks.en: because the Kohanim are not free.
chunks.st: because the priests are not free to do so.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells how they made the keilim of the Beis HaMikdash tahor after Yom Tov. There were extra keilim, so one could be used while another was being toveled.

chunks.en: How did they make the Azarah tahor?
chunks.st: How do they pass all the vessels of the Temple courtyard through a process of purification?

chunks.en: They toveled the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: They immerse the vessels that were in the Temple.

chunks.en: And during Yom Tov they would say to the people,
chunks.st: And they say to the am ha’aretz priests who served in the Temple during the Festival:

chunks.he: הִזָּהֲרוּ שֶׁלֹּא תִגְּעוּ בַּשֻּׁלְחָן וּבַמְּנוֹרָה וּתְטַמְּאוּהוּ.
chunks.en: "Be careful not to touch the Shulchan and the Menorah and make them tamei."
chunks.explain: The Shulchan always had to have the lechem hapanim on it.
chunks.st: Be careful that you not touch the table of the shewbread.
chunks.stMore: If you defile it by touching it, it would need to be removed for immersion, and this would lead to the temporary suspension of the mitzva of the shewbread, which had to be on the table at all times.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's English mentions only the table; the Hebrew also names the Menorah.

words.note: The golden table for the lechem hapanim.

chunks.en: All the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: The mishna continues: All the vessels that were in the Temple

chunks.en: had a second and a third set,
chunks.st: had second and third substitute vessels,

chunks.en: so that if the first ones became tamei,
chunks.st: so that if the first ones became impure

chunks.en: they could bring the second ones instead.
chunks.st: they could bring the second ones in their place.

chunks.en: All the keilim that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: All the vessels that were in the Temple

chunks.en: needed tevilah after Yom Tov,
chunks.st: required immersion after the Festival,

chunks.en: except the golden mizbe'ach and the copper mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: apart from the golden altar and the bronze altar,

chunks.en: because they are like the ground.
chunks.explain: The ground cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: because they are considered like the ground
chunks.stMore: and therefore, like land itself, not susceptible to impurity.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: It is because they are covered with metal.
chunks.st: It is because they are coated.
